title: Marketplace Feature Composition Playbook
author: Leah Nakamura
body:
Overview

This playbook defines the product strategy, implementation requirements, rollout plan, pricing guidance, and release checklist for the "Feature Composition" capability in Redwood's Marketplace. Feature Composition allows customers to assemble multiple serving features (e.g., reranking, embeddings, caching, quantization profiles, and A/B fidelity routes) into composable bundles that behave as single consumable units in the Redwood Console and API. The goal is to accelerate customer time-to-value for common consumption patterns while preserving unit economics and observability.

Goals and success metrics

- Primary goal: Deliver a composable marketplace unit that reduces integration time for customers by 40% and increases bundle adoption rate to 20% of active tenants within 6 months.
- Business metrics: bundle revenue share (% of hosting revenue), avg tokens/sec per bundle, churn delta for customers using bundles, and incremental ARPU.
- Product metrics: time-to-first-bundle (console + API), failure rate for composite executions (<0.5%), average per-token latency delta vs baseline (<10ms).

Key concepts and scope

1) Composition unit: a named, versioned artifact that references one or more Redwood services and configuration profiles (model variant, quantization profile, cache TTLs, routing policy).
2) Execution graph: ordered stages (e.g., preprocessor -> model-A -> reranker -> cache-write) with per-stage SLOs and fallbacks.
3) Consumption contract: public interface (API surface + Console UX) plus pricing model that maps internal resource usage to billable units.
4) Compatibility guarantees: each bundle must include a compatibility matrix that lists supported runtime variants (hosted, dedicated, private) and minimal hardware footprint.

Non-goals

- Not intended to replace low-level SDK primitives. Developers will still be able to call individual services directly.
- No cross-tenant data mixing. Composed bundles adhere to tenant isolation rules and existing KMS/HSM integrations.

High-level product requirements (PRD style)

- PR-1: Bundle lifecycle: create / version / deprecate bundles. Bundles must be immutable once published; patch releases allowed (minor metadata only).
- PR-2: Declarative definition: support YAML/JSON bundle manifest with fields: id, name, description, stages (with service, model_ref, variant, resources), pricing_hint, telemetry_tags. Provide schema and sample manifests.
- PR-3: Execution guarantees: transactions across stages must support partial rollback semantics for idempotent stages; non-idempotent side effects must surface compensating actions in logs and alerts.
- PR-4: Observability: dashboards per-bundle with token-level cost breakdown, per-stage latency heatmaps, and error-trace waterfall.
- PR-5: Console UX: bundle composer with drag/drop stages, validation rules, preflight simulation using synthetic workload.
- PR-6: API: stable REST + SDK endpoints for listing, instantiating, and invoking bundles. Invocation should support streaming responses and function-calling where applicable.
- PR-7: Pricing: define a credit model (see Pricing Guidance section). Price preview in the composer and per-invocation estimate in the API.

Design constraints and decisions

- Decision D-1: Bundles will be first-class entities in the metadata service (service: catalog-api). Bundle manifests are stored versioned in the Config Store (service: cfg-store).
- Decision D-2: Execution will reuse existing runtime components; each stage resolves to an internal route token (route-svc) and executes with tenant-scoped quotas.
- Decision D-3: Bundles must declare a deterministic fallback policy: local-model fallback, variant fallback, regional failover, or degrade-to-sampled-response. The runtime will enforce the first compatible fallback.
- Decision D-4: For Private deployments, customers can opt-in to allow vendor-managed composition or run the composer locally via a CLI that emits a validated manifest.

Compatibility matrix (table-like summary)

- Supported modes: hosted (yes), dedicated (yes), private (opt-in, feature parity v1.1).
- Minimal footprints per composition complexity: small (1 model, no rerank) = 4 vCPU / 16GB GPU memory equivalent; medium (2–3 stages incl reranker) = 8 vCPU / 32GB GPU mem; large (multi-model + embeddings + cache) = 16+ vCPU / multi-GPU.

Runtime orchestration and telemetry

1. Resolution: catalog-api resolves manifest -> stage route tokens -> runtime graph.
2. Execution: running under an execution context that tracks request id, tenant id, trace id, and billing tags.
3. Telemetry: span per-stage with attributes: model_ref, variant, tokens_in/tokens_out, cost_estimate, compute_ms, fallback_triggered.
4. Sampling: include 100% sampling for bundle errors; 1% sampling for success traces (configurable per-tenant).

Pricing guidance and credit model

- Pricing primitive: charge per composite token-equivalent. Each stage contributes a token-weight multiplier based on model size and quantization profile (e.g., small model x1, reranker x0.6 per token, large model x2).
- Bundle-level surcharge: marketplace bundles carry a configurable partner surcharge (0–20%) and optional markup for managed bundles.
- Preview tool: composer shows a 30-day estimate (tokens, compute-hours, estimated credits) based on customer observed traffic patterns or synthetic defaults.

Operational runbook (high-level)

1) On-call flow: bundle execution failures that exceed 0.5% error rate for 10 minutes raise P1 to Runtime and Catalog owners.
2) Quick mitigation steps: toggle bundle to degraded mode (console action: disable external side-effects), route all traffic to variant with highest fidelity fallback.
3) Incident playbook: capture request ids, simulate failing manifest with known-good inputs via the preflight runner, and escalate if rollback not effective within 30 minutes.

Rollout timeline and milestones (quarterly phased)

- Phase 0 (Q4 2028): Internal alpha. Deliver catalog-api schema, composer wireframes, runtime graph prototype, and simple charging calculator.
- Phase 1 (Q1 2029): Private beta with 5 customers; console composer, execution telemetry, pricing-preview.
- Phase 2 (Q2 2029): General availability for hosted and dedicated; partner marketplace onboarding flow.
- Phase 3 (Q3 2029): Marketplace partner launch, revenue tracking, and A/B pricing experiments.

Owner and stakeholders

- Product lead: Leah Nakamura (this doc).
- Engineering owners: Runtime (Riley Chen), Catalog & Config (Marco Reyes), Console/UX (Priya Singh).
- Go-to-market owner: Anya Patel.
- Security/compliance reviewer: Edmund Briggs.

APIs and sample manifests

Sample bundle manifest (YAML) — composer will generate and validate this schema:

```
# bundle-manifest.yaml
id: com.redwood.marketplace.compose.simple-summary-v1
name: "Summary-and-Rerank Bundle"
description: "Generates long-form summary then reranks candidate paragraphs for final selection"
stages:
  - name: summarize
    service: model-svc
    model_ref: open-llama-13b-v2
    variant: quantized-8bit
    resources:
      max_seq: 1024
      batch: auto
  - name: rerank
    service: rerank-svc
    model_ref: reranker-bert-large
    variant: standard
    resources:
      max_candidates: 8
pricing_hint:
  token_multiplier: 1.6
  partner_markup_pct: 10
telemetry_tags:
  - marketplace:feature-composition
  - vertical:knowledge
```

Release checklist (pre-GA)

- [ ] Schema stable and documented in cfg-store.
- [ ] Composer UX: synthetic-preflight and cost-preview integrated.
- [ ] Runtime: per-stage SLO instrumentation and fallback enforcement implemented.
- [ ] Billing: credit calculation validated against 3 traffic profiles.
- [ ] Security: threat model review and data residency checks for Private.
- [ ] Docs: developer guide, sample manifests, SDK examples, and migration notes.

Open questions and risks

- Q1: How to price cross-stage cache benefits (cache reduces compute downstream) without double-counting?
- Q2: Partner revenue share models—should we support revenue splits at invocation time or settlement time?
- Risk: Complexity of composed debugging for customers; mitigation: strong preflight simulator and 1-click trace collection.

Appendix: validation tests and KPIs for GA

- Functional tests: manifest validation, end-to-end execution for 8 canonical manifests, preflight fidelity simulation.
- Performance tests: 95th percentile per-bundle latency under 500 RPS with mixed short/long inputs.
- Billing tests: synthetic load that exercises token multipliers; reconciliation within 0.5% vs expected.
- Customer pilots: onboard 5 customers across e-commerce, knowledge, and support verticals; measure integration time and adoption rates.

If you are reviewing this document: please review the manifest schema section and the pricing_hint model. Flag any backward-incompatible metadata changes before the next sprint cut (2028-11-15).
